title: Withdrawal Planning
blurb: Drawing a corpus down so it lasts: withdrawal rates, inflation, sequence risk, buckets and SWPs.

rows: New employees (all sections), sales team (talk-tracks, role-plays, niche topics); investors as awareness material
About 74 minutes of lessons, plus role-play and the final quiz
Each L.E.A.R.N. stage has: what to know, how to do it, a talk-track, and the investor takeaway

sources: SEBI Master Circular for Mutual Funds (current edition)

lessons.title: Withdrawal rate: how long the money may last
Inflation: why fixed withdrawals feel tighter every year
Before planning: seven facts to gather
Order of withdrawals, and big expenses separate
The one line, and why plans must bend
Compliance: dos, don'ts and the final check

a: Spend from safety, grow from equity, and refill on a plan.
Withdrawal rate, inflation, and the order of returns.
First year’s withdrawal ÷ corpus. ₹4 L from ₹1 Cr = 4%.
At 6%, ₹50,000 of monthly expenses becomes ≈₹90,000 in 10 years.
Losses early in withdrawals do more damage than the same losses later.
Same returns, different order: falls first → runs out ≈ year 19; falls last → ≈₹2.06 Cr left after 20 years.
Systematic Withdrawal Plan: regular redemption of a fixed amount from a fund.
Only the gains part of each withdrawal is a capital gain; depends on fund and holding period. Refer to a CA.
Annual expenses − other income = what the portfolio must provide.
₹6 L expenses − ₹2 L pension and rent = ₹4 L; on ₹1 Cr that is 4%.
Rate above 6–7%, no health cover, no emergency fund, big dependants’ needs, one asset class.
Income (1–2 yrs, liquid), Stability (yrs 3–7, short debt/hybrid), Growth (8+ yrs, equity).
Once a year; take more from equity in good years, less in bad years.
Regular income first, then Bucket 1 SWP, refill on a plan, keep the emergency fund separate.
Rate rose: skip the inflation increase. Markets fell: draw from Bucket 2. Rate fell: modest extra increase.
The total money available for withdrawals.
Example: ₹1 Cr retirement portfolio.
Remember: Count all assets, not just funds.
First year’s withdrawal as % of corpus.
Example: ₹4 L ÷ ₹1 Cr = 4%.
Remember: Small changes matter a lot.
Risk of outliving the money.
Example: Living to 90 on a plan built to 80.
Remember: Plan for the spouse too.
Next 1–2 years of withdrawals.
Example: ₹8–10 L in liquid funds.
Remember: SWP runs from here.
Money for years 3–7.
Example: ₹20–25 L in short-duration debt.
Remember: Pays through bad years.
Money for year 8 onwards.
Example: ₹65–70 L in equity or balanced funds.
Remember: Keeps up with inflation.
The fund the SWP redeems from.
Example: A liquid fund, not small-cap.
Remember: Avoid selling equity monthly.
Day of the month money is paid out.
Example: Just before main bills, after pension.
Remember: Matches cash needs.
Planned yearly rise in withdrawals.
Example: +5–6% a year.
Remember: Review, don’t automate blindly.
Pre-agreed rule to adjust withdrawals.
Example: Skip increase after a big fall.
Remember: Flexibility makes money last.
Money for big known costs.
Example: A child’s wedding in 3 years.
Remember: Not from the monthly SWP.
Medical insurance for client and spouse.
Example: Family floater health policy.
Remember: Biggest risk to a corpus.
Big spending in early retirement.
Example: “Let’s do the big trips now.”
Remember: Use a separate travel pot.
Urge to sell growth assets.
Example: “Move everything to FDs.”
Remember: Buckets 1–2 cover the next years.
Refusing to draw on the corpus.
Example: “I won’t touch it.”
Remember: Show the safe withdrawal amount.
Large gifts or loans to family.
Example: ₹15 L for a son’s business.
Remember: Show the effect on the rate first.

questions.q: How is the withdrawal rate calculated?
questions.why: First year’s withdrawal ÷ corpus. ₹4 L from ₹1 Cr is 4%.

questions.q: In the illustration, about how long does ₹1 Cr last at a 4% rate?
questions.why: 41 years. 9% return and 6% inflation assumed.

questions.q: And at a 6% rate?
questions.why: 21 years. Going from 4% to 6% roughly halves it.

questions.q: At 6% inflation, ₹50,000 of monthly expenses becomes about… in 10 years.
questions.why: ₹90,000. Costs nearly double in about 12 years.

questions.q: Sequence-of-returns risk means…
o: Early losses in withdrawals do more damage
questions.why: Early losses in withdrawals do more damage. Units are sold low to pay bills.

questions.q: Two retirees with the same returns in different order: the one with falls first…
questions.why: Runs out sooner. About year 19 in the illustration.

questions.q: What does an SWP do?
questions.why: Redeems a fixed amount regularly. It is a withdrawal plan, not guaranteed income.

questions.q: Is the whole SWP withdrawal taxed as capital gains?
questions.why: No, only the gains part. Refer details to a CA.

questions.q: Expenses ₹6 L, pension and rent ₹2 L, corpus ₹1 Cr. The withdrawal rate is…
Bucket 1 usually holds…
o: The next 1–2 years of withdrawals in liquid funds
questions.why: The next 1–2 years of withdrawals in liquid funds. The SWP runs from here.

questions.q: Which fund should usually feed the SWP?
questions.why: Liquid or short-duration fund. Avoid selling equity every month.

questions.q: After a sharp market fall, the plan should usually…
questions.why: Draw from Bucket 2. Give equity time to recover.

questions.q: A big known cost (child’s wedding) should be…
questions.why: Planned as a separate pot. Invested for its own date.

questions.q: Which is the biggest threat to many retirement corpuses?
questions.why: Medical costs without health cover. Check health cover.

questions.q: Which statement is compliant?
o: “Illustratively, at 9% assumed and 6% inflation, ₹4 L a year could last about 41 years; not guaranteed.”
questions.why: “Illustratively, at 9% assumed and 6% inflation, ₹4 L a year could last about 41 years; not guaranteed.”. Show assumptions; no guarantees.

questions.q: Should a withdrawal plan start from the client's spending?
o: Yes — expenses minus other income sets the need
questions.why: Expenses minus other income sets the need.

questions.q: Does the order of returns matter once withdrawals start?
o: Yes — early losses do more damage
questions.why: Early losses do more damage.

questions.q: Is an SWP guaranteed monthly income?
o: No — if returns stay below withdrawals, the corpus shrinks
questions.why: If returns stay below withdrawals, the corpus shrinks.

questions.q: Can skipping the inflation increase after a bad year help money last?
o: Yes — flexible spending is a powerful guardrail
questions.why: Flexible spending is a powerful guardrail.

questions.q: Should the emergency fund be used for routine monthly expenses?
questions.why: Keep it separate.

questions.q: Mr. Iyer, 60, has ₹1 Cr, spends ₹6 L a year and gets a ₹2 L pension. What is the plan?
o: SWP of ₹6 L a year from equity
Gap = ₹4 L (4% rate); set up three buckets; SWP from a liquid fund; check health cover; show illustrations with assumptions; no promises
questions.why: Gap = ₹4 L (4% rate); set up three buckets; SWP from a liquid fund; check health cover; show illustrations with assumptions; no promises.

questions.q: Mrs. Rao wants ₹80,000 a month from ₹1 Cr. What do you show her?
o: Show the ≈9.6% rate and how quickly it may run out (illustrative); discuss lower spending, other income or delaying extras
questions.why: Show the ≈9.6% rate and how quickly it may run out (illustrative); discuss lower spending, other income or delaying extras.

questions.q: A new retiree's equity bucket fell 18% and he wants to move all to FDs. What do you do?
o: Move everything to FDs at once
Show Buckets 1–2 cover the next years; avoid selling equity low; apply guardrails; no market predictions
questions.why: Show Buckets 1–2 cover the next years; avoid selling equity low; apply guardrails; no market predictions.

questions.q: A retired client wants to give ₹15 L to her son. How do you handle it?
o: Show the effect on her withdrawal rate and plan; discuss options; it is her decision, documented
Ignore the effect on the plan
Fund it from the monthly SWP
questions.why: Show the effect on her withdrawal rate and plan; discuss options; it is her decision, documented.

questions.q: A client runs his SWP directly from a small-cap fund. What do you change?
o: Nothing — SWPs from equity are ideal
Move the SWP source to a liquid or short-duration fund; refill from equity once a year on a plan
questions.why: Move the SWP source to a liquid or short-duration fund; refill from equity once a year on a plan.
